artworks.title: Yellow-crown Warbler
artworks.artist: Robert Havell after John James Audubon
artworks.medium: hand-colored engraving and aquatint on Whatman wove paper
artworks.creditLine: Gift of Mrs. Walter B. James
artworks.description: This is a painting of three birds perched on a flowering plant. The painting depicts three small birds with distinct plumage patterns and colors interacting with a delicate plant bearing clusters of dark berries and a prominent flower at the top. The birds are finely detailed, showing variations of yellow, blue, green, brown, and white in their feathers. The plant is illustrated with slender, winding stems, and elliptical leaves. The composition is elegant and balanced, highlighting the natural beauty and intricate details of the birds and the plant.

artworks.title: Tennessee Warbler
artworks.artist: Robert Havell after John James Audubon
artworks.medium: hand-colored engraving and aquatint on Whatman wove paper
artworks.creditLine: Gift of Mrs. Walter B. James
artworks.description: This is a painting of a bird perched on a branch with leaves and berries. The painting features a bird with greenish-yellow plumage sitting on a slender branch. Surrounding the bird are green leaves and clusters of small orange-brown berries. The colors and shapes are depicted vividly. The composition is against a plain background, highlighting the detail in the bird and plant. The style is reminiscent of John James Audubon.

artworks.title: Black-throated Blue Warbler
artworks.artist: Robert Havell after John James Audubon
artworks.medium: hand-colored engraving and aquatint on Whatman wove paper
artworks.creditLine: Gift of Mrs. Walter B. James
artworks.description: The image shows a bird with a blue body and black throat perched on a plant with green leaves and pink flowers. The background is light beige.

artworks.title: American Crow
artworks.artist: Robert Havell after John James Audubon
artworks.medium: hand-colored engraving and aquatint on Whatman wove paper
artworks.creditLine: Gift of Mrs. Walter B. James
artworks.description: The American crow is perched on a branch of a tree with clusters of yellow-green fruits and surrounded by elongated green leaves. The color palette consists of black, greens, browns, and yellows. The crow is positioned centrally and slightly towards the left side. Green and leafy branches spread across the image in multiple directions, with a small bird's nest visible lower on the right side.

artworks.title: Rusty Grakle
artworks.artist: Robert Havell after John James Audubon
artworks.medium: hand-colored engraving and aquatint on Whatman wove paper
artworks.creditLine: Gift of Mrs. Walter B. James
artworks.description: Three large birds are perched on a tree branch with dark blue berries and autumn leaves. The birds are brown, bronze, and black. The tree branches are light brown, and the leaves are greenish-yellow and orange.

artworks.title: American Swift
artworks.artist: Robert Havell after John James Audubon
artworks.medium: hand-colored engraving and aquatint on Whatman wove paper
artworks.creditLine: Gift of Mrs. Walter B. James
artworks.description: This is a painting of two birds in flight above their nests. The painting shows two swifts mid-flight, positioned against a neutral background that highlights their detailed plumage. The swift at the top of the image has its wings spread wide, showcasing the variations in hues across its feathers. Below and slightly to the right, another swift flies in a similar manner, its wings slightly angled downwards. Near the bottom of the painting, two nests are depicted. On the left, a nest crafted from twigs and situated within a framework of leaves has an organic, rounded form. To the right, another nest appears to cling to a vertical surface, its structure suspended and creating a sense of hanging precariousness.

artworks.title: Cardinal Grosbeak
artworks.artist: Robert Havell after John James Audubon
artworks.medium: hand-colored engraving and aquatint on Whatman wove paper
artworks.creditLine: Gift of Mrs. Walter B. James

artworks.title: Black-capped Titmouse
artworks.artist: Robert Havell after John James Audubon
artworks.medium: hand-colored engraving and aquatint on Whatman wove paper
artworks.creditLine: Gift of Mrs. Walter B. James
artworks.description: This is a painting of two birds perched on a branch with leaves. The artwork depicts a pair of birds interacting with a cavity in the tree branch. The birds are detailed, with one bird facing upwards towards the nest and the other in a mid-hover position with wings partially extended. Surrounding the birds are lush green leaves and small clusters of white budding flowers. The background is a neutral tone, emphasizing the natural colors of the birds and foliage.

artworks.title: Brasilian Caracara Eagle
artworks.artist: Robert Havell after John James Audubon
artworks.medium: hand-colored engraving and aquatint on Whatman wove paper
artworks.creditLine: Gift of Mrs. Walter B. James
artworks.description: This is a painting of two birds engaging in a dynamic scene. The image portrays one bird perched on a branch with its wings partially extended, while the second bird appears to be swooping down with wings fully spread. Both birds have dark brown, beige, and gray plumage. Their beaks are prominently visible, with hues of pink around the eyes and beak. The detailing of feathers emphasizes movement.

artworks.title: Zenaida Dove
artworks.artist: Robert Havell after John James Audubon
artworks.medium: hand-colored engraving and aquatint on Whatman wove paper
artworks.creditLine: Gift of Mrs. Walter B. James
artworks.description: This is a painting of two doves among flowering branches. The scene features a detailed depiction of one dove perched on a branch with its wings partially open, exhibiting reddish-brown feathers with iridescence, and another dove in flight positioned above the branch, showing a similar rich plumage with a softer brown hue. The doves are surrounded by branches adorned with green leaves and a few blossoming flowers in white and deep red. The painting conveys a sense of natural harmony and precision in capturing the form and color of the birds and foliage.

artworks.title: Palm Warbler
artworks.artist: Robert Havell after John James Audubon
artworks.medium: hand-colored engraving and aquatint on Whatman wove paper
artworks.creditLine: Gift of Mrs. Walter B. James
artworks.description: This is a drawing of two birds perched on a branch of an orange blossom tree. The illustration features a pair of colorful birds with vibrant plumage. One bird is yellow and dynamic, while the other is resting on a smaller branch. The birds are surrounded by green leaves and white blossoms. The drawing is detailed with a focus on naturalistic accuracy.

artworks.title: Tawny Thrush
artworks.artist: Robert Havell after John James Audubon
artworks.medium: hand-colored engraving and aquatint on Whatman wove paper
artworks.creditLine: Gift of Mrs. Walter B. James
artworks.description: The image shows a tawny thrush perched on the foreground next to a cluster of red berries and a tall white and pink flower with slender leaves. The color palette includes earthy browns, muted greens, soft whites, and bright red. The bird is in the center standing on a brown surface, with the berries and leaves in front and to the right, and the flower stem rising behind it.

artworks.title: Bachmans Finch
artworks.artist: Robert Havell after John James Audubon
artworks.medium: hand-colored engraving and aquatint on Whatman wove paper
artworks.creditLine: Gift of Mrs. Walter B. James
artworks.description: This is a painting of a small bird perched on a branch with leafy foliage and delicate flowers. The bird has earthy brown and tan plumage and appears to be inspecting a cluster of round seeds or buds. The branch has large green leaves and clusters of pink-tinged flowers at various stages of blooming and withering. The painting emphasizes fine details such as the textures of the feathers and the veins of the leaves. The background is blank, focusing attention on the bird and plant. The painting is done in the style of John James Audubon.

artworks.title: Rough-legged Falcon
artworks.artist: Robert Havell after John James Audubon
artworks.medium: hand-colored engraving and aquatint on Whatman wove paper
artworks.creditLine: Gift of Mrs. Walter B. James
artworks.description: This is a painting of a rough-legged falcon perched on a branch with its prey. The falcon's talons grip the body of a smaller bird, likely a woodpecker, against the branch. The falcon's feathers show a range of browns, tans, and blacks, with light-colored undersides on its wings and tail. The tree branch has rough bark texture and greenish moss. The background is plain, focusing on the central scene. The style is reminiscent of John James Audubon, known for detailed bird illustrations.

artworks.title: Key-west Dove
artworks.artist: Robert Havell after John James Audubon
artworks.medium: hand-colored engraving and aquatint on Whatman wove paper
artworks.creditLine: Gift of Mrs. Walter B. James
artworks.description: This is a painting of two birds surrounded by greenery and flowers. The image shows two reddish-brown doves, each with wings partially spread, facing each other on the ground. The background features detailed leaves and colorful flowers, including pink and white blossoms. The painting emphasizes the beauty of nature in a harmonious composition.

artworks.title: Forked-tail Flycatcher
artworks.artist: Robert Havell after John James Audubon
artworks.medium: hand-colored engraving and aquatint on Whatman wove paper
artworks.creditLine: Gift of Mrs. Walter B. James
artworks.description: This is a print of a bird perched on a branch with its back to us, surrounded by blooming white flowers. The bird has a long, forked tail and a mix of blue and black plumage, accented with a hint of yellow on its crown and white on its legs and throat. The bird's brown eye is wide open as it looks upward and to the left. The thin brown branch has several white flowers with yellow centers amidst green leaves and small buds. There is a line of text at the bottom of the print.

artworks.title: Mangrove Cuckoo
artworks.artist: Robert Havell after John James Audubon
artworks.medium: hand-colored engraving and aquatint on Whatman wove paper
artworks.creditLine: Gift of Mrs. Walter B. James
artworks.description: This is a painting of a bird on a branch among green leaves and white flowers. The bird has vibrant plumage blending shades of orange and brown, with a long tail marked with black and white patterns. Its wings exhibit a mix of gray and brown hues. The bird is perched on a slender branch among large, lush green leaves, rich in detail with various shades of green and intricate vein patterns. Delicate white flowers with orange centers add contrast to the scene. The composition emphasizes naturalistic elements, capturing the bird and surrounding flora with lifelike precision.

artworks.title: Gray Tyrant
artworks.artist: Robert Havell after John James Audubon
artworks.medium: hand-colored engraving and aquatint on Whatman wove paper
artworks.creditLine: Gift of Mrs. Walter B. James
artworks.description: This is a painting of a gray bird perched on a branch with vibrant red and white flowers and green leaves. The bird, identified as a Gray Tyrant, Tyrannus Griseus, is depicted with remarkable detail, showcasing its soft gray plumage and striking red marking on its head. The surrounding flora consists of elegantly curve-tipped flowers in shades of deep red to crimson, with delicate green tendrils and leaves that provide a lush background.

artworks.title: Barn Owl
artworks.artist: Robert Havell after John James Audubon
artworks.medium: hand-colored engraving and aquatint on Whatman wove paper
artworks.creditLine: Gift of Mrs. Walter B. James
artworks.description: This is print of two barn owls perched on the branches of a leafless tree against a dark sky, with a landscape of a distant river lined with trees visible below. The owl at the top of the painting has its wings spread, and it holds a small brown chipmunk in one claw, gripping the creature's head. The other owl is on a lower branch, and it has its wings partially raised and its beak is open, looking up towards the chipmunk held by the other owl. The feather patterns on both birds are detailed, showing the white on their faces, underbellies, and beneath their wings, as well as the warm brown tones of their heads, backs, and wings. The sky behind them is dark blue-gray.

artworks.title: Blue-headed Pigeon
artworks.artist: Robert Havell after John James Audubon
artworks.medium: hand-colored engraving and aquatint on Whatman wove paper
artworks.creditLine: Gift of Mrs. Walter B. James
artworks.description: Three birds on a rocky surface surrounded by grass and plants. The birds have vibrant blue heads, brown bodies, and some black and white markings. The color palette includes earthy browns, bright blue, rich greens, and pale oranges and reds in the background flora. Two birds are on the lower left, one facing right and the other slightly behind. The third bird is on the right side of the image, standing tall on a rock. Green blades of grass and orange flowers are primarily on the right, with a lighter background representing the sky.

artworks.title: Barn Swallow
artworks.artist: Robert Havell after John James Audubon
artworks.medium: hand-colored engraving and aquatint on Whatman wove paper
artworks.creditLine: Gift of Mrs. Walter B. James
artworks.description: This is a painting of two swallows perched on a nest. The birds are depicted with rich coloring, showcasing their blue feathers and reddish-brown underparts. The nest is crafted from mud and straw, creating intricate texture. The background is minimal, accentuating the focus on the swallows and their nest. This composition highlights the beauty of the birds and their nesting environment. This is in the style of John James Audubon.

artworks.title: Olive-sided Flycatcher
artworks.artist: Robert Havell after John James Audubon
artworks.medium: hand-colored engraving and aquatint on Whatman wove paper
artworks.creditLine: Gift of Mrs. Walter B. James
artworks.description: Two birds are perched on a pine branch with blue-grey pine cones. The birds are gray and brown with white undersides. The color palette includes brown, gray, white, green, and dark blue. One bird is upright on the top left branch, while the other is mid-flight or perched vertically with its head pointing downward on the lower right branch.

artworks.title: Nuttall's Lesser Marsh Wren
artworks.artist: Robert Havell after John James Audubon
artworks.medium: hand-colored engraving and aquatint on Whatman wove paper
artworks.creditLine: Gift of Mrs. Walter B. James
artworks.description: This is a painting of two birds perched on a nest surrounded by tall grass. The painting features two small brown birds situated on a intricately woven nest that is nestled within dense, verdant grass. The birds have detailed plumage with varying shades of brown and are depicted with realistic attention to their feathers and posture. The nest is shown as a carefully crafted bundle of twigs and grass, set amidst tall, slender green blades that fill the composition. The background is left plain, emphasizing the intricacy and realism of the nest and birds.

artworks.title: Spotted Grous
artworks.artist: Robert Havell after John James Audubon
artworks.medium: hand-colored engraving and aquatint on Whatman wove paper
artworks.creditLine: Gift of Mrs. Walter B. James
artworks.description: This is a painting of four birds in a natural setting. The birds are known as "Spotted Grouse" and are portrayed on a grassy and vegetative terrain. They are depicted with detailed brown, black, and white plumage with red accents near their heads. The birds are surrounded by lush green leaves and red berries. The artwork conveys a sense of serenity and harmony, reflecting the birds in their natural habitat. The style of the painting is reminiscent of John James Audubon.
